senses.definition: To produce an air current.
senses.example: Lear. Blow windes, & crack your cheeks; Rage, blow / You Cataracts, and Hyrricano's ſpout,

senses.definition: To propel by an air current (or, if under water, a water current), usually with the mouth.
senses.example: Blow the dust off that book and open it up.

senses.definition: To be propelled by an air current.
senses.example: The leaves blow through the streets in the fall.

senses.definition: To direct or move, usually of a person to a particular location.
senses.example: "This is an unexpected pleasure!" exclaimed he. "What good fortune blows Lady Marchmont hither?"

senses.definition: To create or shape by blowing.
senses.example: to blow bubbles

senses.definition: To force a current of air upon with the mouth, or by other means.
senses.example: to blow the fire

senses.definition: To clear of contents by forcing air through.
senses.example: to blow an egg

senses.definition: To cause to make sound by blowing (as a musical instrument).
senses.example: Blow your horn! That car is about to hit us!

senses.definition: To make a sound as a result of being blown.
senses.example: In the harbor, the ships’ horns blew.

senses.definition: To exhale visibly through the spout the seawater which it has taken in while feeding.
senses.example: There’s nothing more thrilling to the whale watcher than to see a whale surface and blow.

senses.definition: To burst or explode; to occur suddenly
senses.example: Get away from that burning gas tank! It’s about to blow!

senses.definition: To cause to explode, shatter, or be utterly destroyed.
senses.example: The demolition squad neatly blew the old hotel up.

senses.definition: To cause the sudden destruction of.
senses.example: He blew the tires and the engine.

senses.definition: To blow from a gun (method of executing a person).
To suddenly fail or give way destructively.
senses.example: He tried to sprint, but his ligaments blew and he was barely able to walk to the finish line.

senses.definition: Of a vein, to suffer a rupture or puncture in the wall as a result of an injection or cannula, causing fluid (blood, medication, or saline) to leak into the surrounding tissue.
To melt away because of overcurrent, creating a gap in a wire, thus stopping a circuit from operating.
To recklessly squander.
senses.example: I managed to blow $1000 at blackjack in under an hour.

senses.definition: To fail at; to mess up; to make a mistake in.
senses.example: I blew it and forgot to start the spaghetti, so I had plenty of sauce and no pasta.

senses.definition: To be very undesirable.
senses.example: This blows!

senses.definition: To perform oral sex on (someone); to fellate.
senses.example: Who did you have to blow to get those backstage passes?

senses.definition: To leave, especially suddenly or in a hurry.
senses.example: Let’s blow this joint.

senses.definition: To leave the Church of Scientology in an unauthorized manner.
To make flyblown; to defile or spoil, especially with fly eggs.
senses.example:
Shall they hoyſt me vp,
And ſhew me to the ſhowting Varlotarie
Of cenſuring Rome? Rather a ditch in Egypt,
Be gentle graue vnto me, rather on Nylus mudde
Lay me ſtarke-nak'd, and let the water-Flies
Blow me into abhorring;

senses.definition: (of a fly) To lay eggs; to breed (in flesh or meat).
senses.example: […] said the bookseller, “but I cannot risk the expence of your debut - There are critics without as well as within a theatre.” - I know it, said I, interrupting him; “men who, like flies blowing on a piece of wholesome meat, can convert it into carrion - […]

senses.definition: To spread by report; to publish; to disclose.
senses.example: Through the court his courtesy was blown.

senses.definition: To inflate, as with pride; to puff up.
senses.example: O peace, now he's deepely in: looke how imagination blowes him.

senses.definition: To breathe hard or quick; to pant; to puff.
senses.example: Rob. Miſtris Ford, Miſtris Ford: heere's Miſtris Page at the doore, ſsweating, and blowing, and looking wildely, and would needs ſpeake with you preſently.

senses.definition: To put out of breath; to cause to blow from fatigue.
To talk loudly; boast; brag.
senses.example: I don't want the worst characters in hell to be running after me with friendly messages and little testimonials of admiration for Smythe, and blowing about his talents, and bragging on him, and belching their villainous fire and brimstone all through the atmosphere and making my place smell worse than a menagerie.

senses.definition: To slander, insult, critique or discredit (someone); to reprimand or scold (someone).
To expose, or inform on.
senses.example: 'As for that,' says Will, 'I could tell it well enough, if I had it, but I must not be seen anywhere among my old acquaintances, for I am blown, and they will all betray me.'

senses.definition: To sing.
senses.example: That girl has a wonderful voice; just listen to her blow!

senses.definition: To flatulate or defecate.
senses.example: Uh, oh! I gotta blow!

senses.definition: To generate (a reading) on a breath alcohol meter.
senses.example: I blew a zero, so the cop let me drive on.

senses.definition: A strong wind.
senses.example: We’re having a bit of a blow this afternoon.

senses.definition: A chance to catch one's breath.
senses.example: The players were able to get a blow during the last timeout.

senses.definition: Powder cocaine.
senses.example: Hi there, you're a pretty cute chick, want to snort some blow?

senses.definition: Cannabis.
Heroin.
A blowjob; fellatio.

senses.definition: An instance of using high-pressure air to empty water from the ballast tanks of a submarine, increasing the submarine's buoyancy and causing it to surface.
senses.example: The sounding of the alarm was the signal to begin the emergency blow maneuver. At this time, witnesses reported, the guest at the high-pressure air controls operated the levers under close supervision of Navy personnel, and the submarine started to rise at a sharp angle.

senses.definition: Used to express displeasure or frustration.
senses.example: Blow the expense!

senses.definition: Blue.
An instance of the act of striking or hitting.
senses.example: A fabricator is used to direct a sharp blow to the surface of the stone.

senses.definition: A sudden or forcible act or effort; an assault.
senses.example: There he found that […] Hanno's camp was crowded with cattle and carriages, and a mixed multitude of unarmed men, and even of women and children; and that a vigorous blow might win it with all its spoil: the indefatigable general was absent, scouring the country for additional supplies of corn.

senses.definition: A damaging occurrence.
senses.example: A further blow to the group came in 1917 when Thomson died while canoeing in Algonquin Park.

senses.definition: A cut made to a sheep's fleece by a shearer using hand-shears.
senses.example: Click goes his shears; click, click, click. / Wide are the blows, and his hand is moving quick, / The ringer looks round, for he lost it by a blow, / And he curses that old shearer with the bare belled ewe.

senses.definition: An outcrop of quartz from surrounding rock, thought to indicate mineral deposits below.
senses.example: "Blows" of quartz, crop out above the layers of slate, granite, and sandstone formation.

senses.definition: Synonym of button (“the punchy or suspenseful line of dialogue that concludes a scene”).
senses.example: The blow is important because it transitions the reader and eventually the audience from one scene to another.

senses.definition: To blossom; to cause to bloom or blossom.
senses.example: You ſeeme to me as Diane in her Orbe, / As chaſte as is the budde ere it be blowne:

senses.definition: A state of flowering; a bloom.
senses.example: roses in full blow

senses.definition: A display or mass of flowers; a yield.
senses.example: [H]e believed he could shew me such a blow of tulips as was not to be matched in the whole country.

senses.definition: A display of anything bright or brilliant.
A surname.
